extracted.intended_audience: offshore renewable-energy developers, industry stakeholders, and members of the public preparing comments on BOEM's proposed Renewable Energy Modernization Rule
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory text describing a proposed revision to 30 CFR part 585 (Renewable Energy on the OCS) and instructions for submitting public comments on that proposed rule. Includes procedural guidance for commenters and substantive regulatory requirements applicants/lessees must meet (SAP/COP/GAP, CVA, financial assurance, inspections, decommissioning, leasing/auctions, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit comments regarding the substance of this proposed rule to BOEM on or before March 31, 2023. Submit comments regarding the information collection burden of this proposed rule to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and to BOEM on or before March 1, 2023. Comments received after these dates might not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness is a threshold requirement: substantive comments should be submitted by the rule's comment deadline; information-collection-specific comments must meet the earlier OMB/BOEM deadline. Late comments 'might not be considered.'

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit comments / addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for submitting comments include the Federal e-rulemaking portal (https://www.regulations.gov) and U.S. Postal Service/other mail delivery to the Office of Regulations, BOEM (attention Georgeann Smale). Information-collection comments can also be submitted via https://www.reginfo.gov and by emailing or mailing a copy to the Information Collection Clearance Officer (Anna Atkinson).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing via regs.gov, follow the site's instructions; helpful search terms are 'RIN 1010-AE04' or 'BOEM-2022-0019.' For information-collection comment submission, follow the steps listed (select Dept. of the Interior, find OMB Control Number 1010-0176 or 1010-NEW as applicable). Provide a copy of information-collection comments to BOEM's clearance officer and reference the OMB control number in the subject line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference docket number and RIN in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments submitted regarding this proposed rule and its information collection requirements should reference the docket number BOEM-2022-0019 or RIN 1010-AE04.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly include the docket number or RIN in your submission so it is associated with the correct rulemaking docket; omission may complicate agency consideration or docketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and protection of personally identifiable information (PII)
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received by BOEM will be reviewed and may be posted to https://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided with the submission. Agencies may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include confidential business information or unnecessary PII in comments. For instructions on submitting comments and protecting PII, see the 'What Should I Consider as I Prepare My Comments?' subsection (II.A) of the Supplementary Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: What should I consider as I prepare my comments? (Section II.A headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section II.A of the preamble lists topics commenters should consider: 1. Contact Information; 2. Public Availability of Comments; 3. Information Collection Comments; 4. Scope of Comments; 5. Suggestions for Preparing Your Comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble points readers to Section II.A for specific instructions and considerations when preparing comments; see that subsection for detail on scope, formats, contact info, and other submission suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed elimination of SAP requirement for met buoys
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would eliminate the Site Assessment Plan (SAP) requirement for deployment of meteorological (met) buoys (both on-lease and off-lease limited-lease requirement), because met buoys gather the same data at lower cost and with less environmental impact than fixed met towers and BOEM's SAP process is redundant with USACE permit processes for buoys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although BOEM proposes to remove its SAP approval requirement for met buoys, met buoys deployed in navigable waters remain subject to U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) permits under section 10 of the Rivers and Harbors Act; a commercial lessee seeking to install a met tower would still need to submit a SAP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increased flexibility for geophysical and geotechnical surveys
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would defer certain geotechnical survey requirements (e.g., engineering site-specific surveys such as boreholes, vibracores, grab samplers, cone penetrometer tests and other penetrative methods) so that detailed engineering surveys may be submitted after COP approval but before construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change reflects industry concerns that precise turbine locations may be uncertain at the COP submittal stage; BOEM's guidance for geotechnical surveys is available online and geophysical/geotechnical submission rules are adjusted to allow more time and flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Design Envelope and phased approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule addresses use of a Project Design Envelope in a Construction and Operations Plan (COP) to allow flexibility in final project design while providing BOEM the data needed to complete environmental review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM references prior draft guidance and technical reports on phased approaches and PDEs; commenters may address how PDEs affect environmental review, analysis adequacy, and design certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified Verification Agent (CVA) role and verification standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would expand the CVA's role to include verification of the design and commissioning of critical safety systems and change regulatory language from 'certify'/'certification' to 'verify'/'verification' to align with industry practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CVA duties (nominating, primary duties for facility design review, fabrication and installation review, onsite verification, reporting requirements) are set out in proposed changes (see §585.705–§585.712). BOEM would require CVA or project engineer verification where facilities are complex and significant; BOEM is 'deemed' to have no objections if it does not object within 60 days of receiving reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewable energy leasing schedule and related changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule revises the Renewable Energy Leasing Schedule (Subpart B) to modernize how BOEM establishes and uses the schedule for offshore renewable energy leasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses existing regulations, why they should be updated, and proposed changes to the leasing schedule; commenters can address the schedule's frequency, transparency, geographic priorities, and alignment with demand and environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease issuance procedures, auctions, and bidding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart C revises issuance of OCS renewable energy leases, including competitive lease award process (pre-auction, auction, post-auction provisions), auction processes and rules, multiple factor auctions and bidding credits, improper or inappropriate bidder communications, provisional winner obligations, and re-offering leases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule details steps in BOEM's competitive award process (Call, area identification, PSN/FSN content), auction general provisions, supplemental information, and actions if provisional winners fail obligations; commenters may address auction design, fairness, bidder eligibility, communications policies, and re-offer procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk management and financial assurance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart F revises payments and financial assurance requirements, including deposits for competitive leases, rent and operating fee rules, staged funding of decommissioning accounts, supplemental financial assurance determinations, permitted instruments other than surety bonds (e.g., third-party guaranties, decommissioning accounts), credit-rating considerations, joint and several liability, and conditions for forfeiture or cancellation of financial assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed changes include elimination of COP-approval financial assurance requirement, revisions to lease-specific financial-assurance amounts, additional authorized instruments, staged funding, and circumstances under which BOEM may call forfeiture; commenters may address sufficiency of assurances, instruments' reliability, and economic impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans and information requirements (SAP, COP, GAP) and processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart G specifies what plans and information must be submitted (Site Assessment Plan/SAP, Construction and Operations Plan/COP, General Activities Plan/GAP), timing for submissions, records to maintain, required contents of SAP/COP/GAP (including survey, environmental, and certification information), NEPA and other statutory compliance certifications, Federal consistency under the Coastal Zone Management Act, processing timelines, required revisions, and activities allowed under approved plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule standardizes presentation of required content (general informational requirements and survey/investigation data), clarifies when activities may commence under approved plans, and specifies when revisions are required; COP requirements include COP data elements (see §585.621, §585.626, §585.627, §585.628).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility design, fabrication, and installation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H identifies required reports (Facility Design Report/FDR, Fabrication and Installation Report/FIR), what each report must include, reporting for project modifications and repairs, BOEM's review process for FDRs and FIRs, and recordkeeping requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports are tied to CVA reviews; when CVA or BOEM raise concerns, lessees must address them before installations may begin. BOEM may be 'deemed' to have no objections if it does not respond within statutory review periods. Record retention provisions for FDR/FIRs and verification reporting are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Management Systems (SMS) and incident reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart I requires submission of a Safety Management System (when required), what must be included in an SMS, whether SMS certification is required, implementation expectations, equipment-failure and adverse-environment reporting, inspections and assessments (BOEM-conducted and self-inspections), and incident reporting and investigation obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule clarifies timing and content of SMS submissions (see §§585.810–585.812), requirements for self-inspections, how BOEM conducts scheduled and unscheduled inspections, what lessees/operators must do during inspections, and incident-reporting timelines and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspections: BOEM and self-inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: BOEM may conduct inspections (scheduled and unscheduled) and requires lessees and grant holders to conduct self-inspections in specified circumstances. The rule describes what lessees must do when BOEM conducts an inspection and how self-inspection programs should be structured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed changes include clarifying BOEM inspection authority and self-inspection requirements; commenters may address frequency, scope, confidentiality of inspection findings, and interaction with OSHA reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decommissioning obligations and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart J sets decommissioning obligations (who must meet them), general decommissioning requirements for facilities authorized under SAP/COP/GAP, timing for decommissioning applications and required contents, and coordination with other agencies' decommissioning obligations (e.g., FERC or National Marine Sanctuaries permits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed rule includes options for staged funding of decommissioning accounts and clarifies responsibilities for alternate-use RUE facilities; commenters may address sufficiency of decommissioning funding mechanisms and timing of applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights-of-Use and Easement (RUE) for alternate use of existing OCS facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart K explains how to request an Alternate Use RUE, the process for RUE applications, and decommissioning responsibilities for OCS facilities used for energy- and marine-related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule clarifies when an alternate-use RUE is appropriate, what information must be submitted (see §585.1005 et seq.), and who bears decommissioning responsibility for facilities located on an Alternate Use RUE (see §585.1018).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural matters and statutory/regulatory analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Section VII lists statutes and executive orders relevant to the proposed rule (NEPA, Paperwork Reduction Act, Regulatory Flexibility Act, Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act, Unfunded Mandates Reform Act, Congressional Review Act, and multiple Executive Orders) and explains procedural analyses (Regulatory Impact Analysis, IRIA) and public-inspection information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters may reference these statutes/EOs when addressing legal or economic issues and when submitting information-collection burden comments (including referencing the proposed ICR and OMB control numbers). The preamble provides links and references to supporting analyses and the rule's docket for supporting documents.
